reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: A distinctive facial gestalt with synophrys (confluent eyebrows), long philtrum, thin down-turned upper lip, and long curly eyelashes is the diagnostic hallmark
Prenatal and postnatal growth restriction with microcephaly is characteristic and often severe
Upper-limb reduction defects range from small hands with proximally placed thumbs to severe oligodactyly or phocomelia
Generalised hirsutism, a low anterior and posterior hairline, and cutis marmorata are frequently seen
Most cases follow autosomal dominant inheritance from de novo NIPBL variants, with X-linked (SMC1A, HDAC8) and other cohesin-related genes accounting for milder phenotypes
Gastro-oesophageal reflux is common and easily overlooked, and can drive irritability, feeding refusal and self-injurious behaviour
Intellectual disability, autistic features, and expressive language deficits are typical, with severity broadly tracking the causative gene and mutation type
reference.pathophysiology: Cornelia de Lange syndrome is a cohesinopathy caused by dysfunction of the cohesin complex or its regulators, which normally hold sister chromatids together and also regulate transcription and chromatin architecture. Loss-of-function or missense variants in NIPBL (the commonest) or in the structural and regulatory subunits SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21 and HDAC8 disturb the expression of developmental gene networks. This dysregulation during embryogenesis produces the multisystem pattern of growth failure, limb reduction, craniofacial malformation and neurodevelopmental impairment. Somatic mosaicism is well recognised and can lead to false-negative blood testing.
additionalInvestigations: Targeted gene-panel or exome sequencing covering NIPBL, SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21 and HDAC8
Testing of tissues such as buccal cells or fibroblasts when mosaicism is suspected despite negative blood results
Chromosomal microarray to exclude copy-number mimics
Echocardiography to detect congenital heart disease
Upper gastrointestinal evaluation and monitoring for reflux and malrotation
Hearing and ophthalmology assessment including for ptosis and refractive error
redFlags: Unexplained irritability or feeding refusal suggesting severe gastro-oesophageal reflux or oesophagitis
Cyanosis or poor feeding indicating an undiagnosed congenital heart defect
Bilious vomiting raising concern for intestinal malrotation with volvulus
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies widely with genotype and severity; individuals with classic NIPBL-related disease often have significant intellectual disability and medical comorbidity, whereas milder variants permit better cognitive and functional outcomes. Life expectancy is largely determined by cardiac, gastrointestinal and respiratory complications.
pitfalls: Excluding the diagnosis on a negative blood test when tissue mosaicism can still be present
Attributing behavioural disturbance to the syndrome itself and missing treatable reflux or pain
Overlooking hearing loss that compounds language delay
Failing to screen for occult congenital heart disease and genitourinary anomalies
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
Kline et al. Consensus statement on diagnosis and management of Cornelia de Lange syndrome
